questionText: Which one of the following statements is FALSE?
options: In the cycle stealing mode of DMA, one word of data is transferred between an I/O device and main memory in a stolen cycle
For bulk data transfer, the burst mode of DMA has a higher throughput than the cycle stealing mode
Programmed I/O mechanism has a better CPU utilization than the interrupt driven I/O mechanism
The CPU can start executing an interrupt service routine faster with vectored interrupts than with non-vectored interrupts
explanation:
Analysis of each statement:

(A) True: In cycle stealing mode, the DMA controller transfers one word of data at a time by 'stealing' a bus cycle from the CPU.

(B) True: Burst mode transfers a continuous block of data without giving control back to the CPU until the transfer completes, leading to higher throughput for bulk data transfers compared to cycle stealing mode.

(C) False: Programmed I/O uses busy-waiting (polling), where the CPU continuously checks the status of the I/O device, resulting in very poor CPU utilization. Interrupt-driven I/O allows the CPU to execute other tasks while waiting for I/O, leading to much better CPU utilization.

(D) True: In vectored interrupts, the interrupt source provides the memory address of the Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) directly, enabling faster branch execution compared to non-vectored interrupts where the CPU must poll/determine the source first.

Hence, statement (C) is FALSE.
